name: Enavatuzumab
sponsor: Facet Biotech / PDL BioPharma -> Abbott -> AbbVie Biotherapeutics
agonist_antagonist: inhibits tumour cell growth and induces ADCC; no IL8/cell-death agonism alone, but oligomerisation or FcgR binding converts it into a potent agonist
internalization_evidence: not established in the sources read
epitope_method: loses binding to R56P, retains binding to W42A (Salzmann 2013 Fig 1A, FACS on Hek293; full text read by this project). The mutations themselves do not interfere with TWEAK binding.
competes_with_TWEAK: NO - practically no competition with TWEAK for Fn14 binding (Salzmann 2013 Fig 1F)
notes: Parent mouse mAb 19.2.1 (IgG2a). Does NOT bind murine Fn14. Phase 1 DLTs were grade 3-4 lipase, amylase and bilirubin elevations. v1 of this table wrongly assigned both W42 and R56 to this antibody.

name: P4A8
modality: mouse parental mAb; scFv used in immunotoxins
sponsor: academic (Wuerzburg) / Biogen Idec lineage; Tehran Univ. Med. Sci. for the immunotoxins
agonist_antagonist: not agonistic alone; strongly agonistic after oligomerisation or FcgR binding
internalization_evidence: implied by immunotoxin activity, not directly measured in the sources read
epitope_method: loses binding to W42A, retains binding to R56P (Salzmann 2013 Fig 1A; full text read by this project)
competes_with_TWEAK: YES - efficiently inhibits GpL-TWEAK binding (Salzmann 2013 Fig 1F)
notes: Also named mBIIB036. Key counter-example: W42 is NOT buried by TWEAK in the M2 model, yet this antibody blocks TWEAK - so single-residue burial cannot predict competition. What does separate it from PDL192 is orientation (47 deg vs 139 deg from the footprint); see results_v2 section 3.

name: BIIB036
agonist_antagonist: agonist: induces Fn14 signalling and apoptosis in vitro; needs full Fc effector function and higher valency for maximal in vivo effect
internalization_evidence: not established in the sources read
epitope_method: no residue-level mapping of the humanized form; but its OWN competition experiment is E3 by the frozen ladder: reciprocal dose-dependent competition with TWEAK on WiDr colon carcinoma cells (Michaelson 2011 Fig 2B). It does not inherit P4A8's W42 mapping.
species_tested: human, mouse, rat and cynomolgus Fn14 (Michaelson 2011 Fig 2A)
competes_with_TWEAK: YES - dose-dependent, and reciprocal (TWEAK also blocks BIIB036), in WiDr colon carcinoma cells (Michaelson 2011 Fig 2B)
notes: Michaelson 2011 full text: "The murine antibody mBIIB036 (P4A8) ... was subsequently humanized by CDR grafting to generate a drug candidate, BIIB036, with a human IgG1 backbone." Same lineage as FNB-002; counted once, not as an independent epitope finding.

name: ITEM-4
modality: mouse mAb (research reagent); scaffold for several conjugates
agonist_antagonist: weak agonistic activity (Cheng 2013 review, open access)
internalization_evidence: not established for the naked antibody; the 2 h internalisation result is for the ITEM4-rGel conjugate (FNB-012)
epitope_method: high-affinity binder; no residue mapping in the sources read
species_tested: human and mouse Fn14 (ITEM4 raised against the human Fn14 ECD; binds both - Cheng 2013)
competes_with_TWEAK: not established in the sources read

name: 18D1
agonist_antagonist: becomes a strong agonist on oligomerisation or FcgR binding
internalization_evidence: not established in the sources read
epitope_method: blocks TWEAK binding at 0.2-2 ug/ml; binds W42A and R56P efficiently, so its epitope differs from both LIN-19.2.1 and LIN-P4A8
notes: ADCC-enhanced and ADCC-defective variants both reduced liver metastasis in a human colon carcinoma xenograft; only the ADCC-enhanced variant suppressed lung metastasis in RENCA.

name: 4G5
agonist_antagonist: becomes a strong agonist on oligomerisation or FcgR binding
internalization_evidence: not established in the sources read
epitope_method: blocks TWEAK binding at 0.2-2 ug/ml; binds W42A and R56P efficiently

name: 5B6
agonist_antagonist: becomes a strong agonist on oligomerisation or FcgR binding
internalization_evidence: not established in the sources read
epitope_method: does NOT efficiently block TWEAK binding; binds W42A and R56P efficiently
notes: Binds Fn14 without blocking TWEAK, so its epitope is likely away from the TWEAK footprint. Distinct clone from 18D1/4G5: same discovery campaign, different lineage, and the functional split (5B6 does not block) is why they must not share a lineage id.

name: TWEAKR-KSPi-ADC1 / ADC2
binder_lineage_id: not stated in the sources read
modality: ADC (mAb + small-molecule kinesin spindle protein inhibitor)
agonist_antagonist: not characterised in the sources read
internalization_evidence: YES per the GPT review citing the 2018 KSPi ADC study (Kd ~13 nM, TWEAKR-dependent internalisation); NOT independently verified
internalization_verification_status: unverified (review-transcribed figure; not read by this project)
competes_with_TWEAK: not established in the sources read
notes: THE Fn14 ADC that v1 of this table missed, because Bayer indexes the target as TWEAKR, not Fn14. Strong efficacy in a TWEAKR-expressing CT26 COLON cancer model; at suboptimal doses it worked only in immunocompetent mice, indicating an additional immunological mechanism. Most CRC-relevant entry in this table.

name: GrB-Fc-IT4
binder_lineage_id: LIN-ITEM4 (humanized scFv; relationship stated in review, not in the abstract)
modality: granzyme B fusion (human serine protease payload)
agonist_antagonist: not characterised in the sources read
internalization_evidence: YES per the GPT review citing Zhou 2014 Fig 2B (cytosolic entry in Fn14-positive HT-29); NOT independently verified
internalization_verification_status: unverified (review-transcribed figure; not read by this project)
competes_with_TWEAK: not established in the sources read
notes: Uses a humanized anti-Fn14 single-chain antibody as the targeting moiety. Also identified Fn14 as overexpressed in triple-negative breast cancer.

name: hSGZ
agonist_antagonist: not characterised in the sources read
internalization_evidence: YES per the GPT review citing Zhou 2013 imaging (Fig 1A/2F); NOT independently verified by this project
internalization_verification_status: unverified (review-transcribed figure; not read by this project)
competes_with_TWEAK: not established in the sources read
notes: Cheng 2013 (open access, read by this project): both MD Anderson immunotoxins are based on the anti-Fn14 antibody ITEM4 and the plant toxin gelonin. The LIN-ITEM4 assignment is therefore first-hand, not review-only.

name: ITEM4-rGel
internalization_evidence: YES: internalises specifically and rapidly (within 2 h) in Fn14-positive T-24 cells, not in Fn14-deficient fibroblasts (confocal, Zhou 2011)
internalization_verification_status: verified (Zhou 2011 abstract read by this project)
competes_with_TWEAK: not established in the sources read
notes: 8- to 80000-fold more potent than free gelonin across 22 tumour lines.
